candidates.original_title: Wheelchair control by elderly participants in a virtual environment with a brain-computer interface (BCI) and tactile stimulation
candidates.description: Training effects on BCI performance (ITR and online accuracy) and P300 physiological measures during virtual wheelchair navigation using tactile stimulation
candidates.citation_sentence: We present a slightly adapted and extended replication of the study by Herweg et al. (2016).
candidates.notes: The paper reports both confirmed training effects (H2: ITR increased significantly) and non-confirmed hypotheses (H3: not all participants reached 70% efficiency; H4: age was a limiting factor). Overall performance was lower than the original study (Herweg et al., 2016). The replication is described as 'slightly adapted and extended' with individualized sequence numbers and a non-elderly sample. The paper confirms H2 (training increases ITR and accuracy significantly) but rejects H3 (70% accuracy threshold not met by all participants) and H4 (age did affect performance, with middle-aged group underperforming). The original Herweg et al. (2016) reported very high performance in elderly participants; this replication found high discrepancies and many inefficient participants. Mixed pattern of confirming and disconfirming findings relative to the original.
